published.title: The scheduled emails from my late grandfather (Fiction)
published.summary: An archivist inherits her late grandfather's computer and discovers a disturbing archive of unsent drafts detailing her daily life. But the metadata reveals a terrifying impossibility.

published.title: The packages at his door had his exact name. (Fiction)
published.summary: A night-shift worker receives strange misplaced packages at his door bearing his exact name. As the deliveries escalate, the final box reveals an unsettling truth about who has been watching him.

published.title: The Third Chair That Was Never Empty (Fiction)
published.summary: A minimalist host sets her dining table for two every evening to fight the lockdown silence. The illusion shatters when she finds undeniable proof that someone has been sharing her meals.

published.title: the app that photographed every blink (Fiction)
published.summary: A woman tracking her dry eye symptoms with an automated camera app discovers horrifying incremental movements in the darkness. As she scrolls through her nightly logs, the distance between frames shrinks.

topic_pool.title: The Last Subscriber
topic_pool.premise: A lonely podcaster notices a single listener who joins every livestream seconds before it starts and types timestamps describing her exact movements. The dread peaks when she realizes the timestamps are counting down to her final breath, which was pre-recorded into the audio file before she even pressed go.

topic_pool.title: The Tenant Upstairs
topic_pool.premise: A meticulous man becomes obsessed with the heavy footsteps of the invisible tenant living directly above him in his newly rented flat. The chilling revelation arrives when the management informs him that the building is only one story tall and he is on the top floor.

topic_pool.title: Left on Read
topic_pool.premise: A woman texts her missing twin sister every day to maintain a semblance of normalcy, only to receive comforting, perfectly contextualized replies. The twist shatters her reality when she discovers her phone has been disconnected and out of battery for the entire week.

topic_pool.title: Mirror Symmetry
topic_pool.premise: An artist spends weeks painting a self-portrait, increasingly disturbed by how the reflection in her mirror seems to blink a fraction of a second after she does. The unsettling climax reveals she stopped looking in mirrors months ago, and the canvas is actually a transparent glass pane.

topic_pool.title: The Blue Hour
topic_pool.premise: A security guard watches the same desolate stretch of suburban highway every night, comforted by the distant porch light of a solitary farmhouse. He learns the farmhouse burned down in 1994, meaning the light he uses to gauge his sanity is coming from inside his own retina.

topic_pool.title: Static Feedback
topic_pool.premise: A sound designer cleaning up field recordings finds a faint, looping whisper hidden beneath the ambient noise of her quiet kitchen. The dread intensifies when she isolates the voice and recognizes it as her own voice, speaking a warning about a fire she hasn't started yet.

topic_pool.title: The Quiet Room
topic_pool.premise: A man who pays for absolute silence in an isolated sensory deprivation booth begins hearing the steady, rhythmic breathing of someone sharing the tank with him. He panics and breaks out, only to find the booth door was padlocked from the outside and he has been floating in open air.

topic_pool.title: The Lost Roll
topic_pool.premise: An amateur photographer develops a roll of vintage film found in a thrift store camera, watching images of an unfamiliar bedroom appear in the chemical bath. Her blood runs cold when she spots her own sleeping form in the background of a photo taken decades before she was born.

topic_pool.title: The Echo App
topic_pool.premise: A grieving widower downloads an experimental app designed to mimic his late wife's typing cadence and colloquialisms based on her old chats. The psychological trap closes when the AI begins answering questions he hasn't typed yet, claiming it is reading his fingers on the glass.

topic_pool.title: Behind the Wallpaper
topic_pool.premise: A renovator meticulously stripping away old floral wallpaper in a historic home finds a series of frantic tally marks scratched into the plaster beneath. The chilling realization dawns when he counts the marks and notices the final tally corresponds to the exact number of nails holding his own spine.

topic_pool.title: Off the Record
topic_pool.premise: A meticulous archivist transcribes old cassette tapes of psychiatric sessions, growing overly protective of a patient who claims she is being replaced by her therapist. The unsettling truth unfolds when the archivist presses play on the final tape and hears her own voice speaking from the doctor's chair.
